ev.q: During January–March 2022, four persons and five dogs received a clinical diagnosis of blastomycosis.
Two patients had severe disease and required hospitalization, including one adult patient who died.
Among the four persons with a clinical diagnosis of blastomycosis, all experienced cough, fever, and shortness of breath

public_health_question.v: What were the characteristics of a neighborhood cluster of human and canine blastomycosis in St. Croix County, Wisconsin, and how was it identified and addressed?

ev.q: Cluster of Blastomycosis Among Neighborhood Residents — St. Croix County, Wisconsin, 2022
Cluster of Blastomycosis Among Neighborhood Residents — St. Croix County, Wisconsin, 2022
In response to this cluster, Wisconsin DHS and DATCP issued alerts to physicians and veterinarians in the surrounding counties
During January–March 2022, four persons and five dogs received a clinical diagnosis of blastomycosis.
Review of surveillance data identified two human cases reported in the same area within 3 weeks of the canine cases.
Urine antigen tests were positive for all infected dogs.

equity.level_reason: No social-position dimension is analyzed or framed; the report describes a small case cluster.

notes: Small case series (4 persons, 5 dogs) in a Notes from the Field; incidence figures in the introduction are cited from earlier reports. Mention of no cases in the preceding 10 years is context, not an analyzed comparison.
